workflow.title: Declare
workflow.detail: Define a supported material response or coupled weak form in Python.

workflow.title: Check the Python model
workflow.detail: Check tangent consistency and compare selected responses with an analytical or independently implemented reference.

workflow.title: Generate Fortran
workflow.detail: Write deterministic, self-contained fixed-form Fortran for inspection and compilation.

workflow.title: Verify generated code
workflow.detail: Compile and call the generated UMAT or UEL. Compare the returned stress and state values, or UEL residual and tangent blocks, with the Python reference.

workflow.title: Run in Abaqus
workflow.detail: Use the generated subroutine in an Abaqus model with documented mesh, steps, loads, units, solver controls, and output checks.

scopes.title: Material response
scopes.description: Supported finite- and small-strain constitutive declarations, including state-variable updates between increments and Abaqus stress and tangent conventions.
scopes.boundary: The UMAT generator does not select the Abaqus element, procedure, mesh, load history, or material calibration.

scopes.title: Coupled-field elements
scopes.description: Residual and tangent generation for supported coupled fields, interpolation orders, constitutive laws, and condensed local variables.
included: mixed-order interpolation and condensed local pressure
scopes.boundary: The UEL generator supports the listed formulations; it does not accept arbitrary variational expressions or generate a complete Abaqus analysis.

examples.title: Neo-Hookean
examples.summary: Finite-strain material without state variables; the UMAT returns Cauchy stress and an Abaqus Jaumann DDSDDE.
examples.evidence: Closed-form uniaxial and shear checks, deterministic regeneration, agreement between the compiled UMAT and Python response, and a finite-difference check of the Abaqus tangent.
examples.boundary: No Abaqus solver run is retained with this example.

examples.title: Small-strain J2
examples.summary: Small-strain J2 plasticity with radial return, elastic and plastic branches, STATEV updates, and engineering-shear ordering.
examples.evidence: Closed-form shear check and agreement between the compiled UMAT and a 40-increment Python stress and STATEV history.
examples.boundary: No Abaqus solver run is retained with this example.

examples.title: Viscoelasticity
examples.summary: Time-step-dependent viscoelastic update with tensor history stored in STATEV.
examples.evidence: Exact discrete-relaxation check and agreement between the compiled UMAT and a 30-increment Python history.
examples.boundary: No Abaqus solver run is retained with this example.

examples.title: Ogden spectral path
examples.summary: Finite-strain Ogden response evaluated by spectral decomposition, including repeated principal stretches.
examples.evidence: Checks independent of eigenvector choice, agreement between compiled and Python responses, and finite-difference tangent checks for distinct and repeated principal stretches.
examples.boundary: No Abaqus solver run is retained with this example.

examples.title: Thermo-mechanical Quad4
examples.summary: Two-field displacement-temperature element with cross-field blocks and node-interleaved DOFs.
examples.evidence: Closed-form nodal-force and heat-balance checks, agreement between compiled UEL and Python residual and tangent calculations, and a one-element Abaqus 2022 run.
examples.boundary: This is a one-element Abaqus check, not a general thermo-mechanical validation.

examples.title: Mixed-order Quad8
examples.summary: Quadratic displacement with bilinear corner temperature and deformation-dependent pulled-back flux.
examples.evidence: Independent pulled-back-flux ratio check, Python and compiled residual and tangent checks, and a one-element Abaqus 2022 run.
examples.boundary: This is a one-element Abaqus check, not a paper-scale analysis.

paperEvidence.title: Stabilized mixed u–θ Tet4
paperEvidence.summary: Quarter-block compression using the kinematically stabilized equal-order tetrahedron of Scovazzi, Zorrilla, and Rossi.
paperEvidence.result: The completed n=16 run gives u₃ = −0.696244 mm at full follower pressure, within about 1% of the published n=16 curve.
paperEvidence.freshCheck: The current source was regenerated and compiled; the tracked n=16 deck passed datacheck. A generated n=2 model completed 24 increments with zero cutbacks.
paperEvidence.boundary: The full n=16 analysis was not repeated during the 2026-07-30 release check.

paperEvidence.title: Diffusion-driven morphing sequence
paperEvidence.summary: A Hex8 UEL models a grooved gel sheet with nodal displacement and chemical potential and one condensed pressure variable per element.
paperEvidence.result: The package includes six Abaqus/CAE frames and reduced ODB snapshots from the completed production run.
paperEvidence.freshCheck: The archived production source and deck passed Abaqus 2022 datacheck. The current generator separately passed its local-pressure residual and tangent checks.
paperEvidence.boundary: The production analysis was not rerun. The production model also contains a shared-node C3D8 mesh that contributes stiffness; its effect has not yet been quantified.

paperEvidence.title: Mixed-order gel bilayer
paperEvidence.summary: Plane-strain swelling with quadratic displacement and chemical potential, bilinear corner pressure, and 28 element DOFs.
paperEvidence.result: The package includes the accepted deck and four historical Abaqus/CAE exports at 0, 30 min, 1 h, and 6 h; it does not include a full-run solver log or machine-readable result record.
paperEvidence.freshCheck: One- and two-element gel models generated from the current source completed in Abaqus/Standard 2022 with zero cutbacks.
paperEvidence.boundary: The full bilayer was not rerun. Regenerating its deck requires the separately obtained Chester–Di Leo–Anand mesh seed; their original supplemental files are not redistributed.

paperEvidence.title: Phase-field corrosion comparison
paperEvidence.summary: Three-field displacement–phase-field–concentration Quad8 declaration compared with the Cui–Ma–Martínez-Pañeda reference implementation.
paperEvidence.result: The package includes the reference pit-depth history, final field data, and comparison summaries retained from the earlier runs.
paperEvidence.freshCheck: Both Fortran variants were regenerated and compiled. The tracked full input with the regenerated diagonal UEL passed Abaqus 2022 datacheck.
paperEvidence.boundary: The full analysis was not rerun. The comparison mesh came from a third-party distribution whose complete BSD license notice has not been located, so its redistribution status remains unresolved.
